query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled minor addition of Nb (below 1 wt%) into a eutectic high-entropy alloy followed by a tailored thermal processing step to promote Nb segregation to the internal lamellar boundaries will enhance both tensile strength and room-temperature ductility relative to the conventional unmodified alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy characterized by dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries that serve as microcracking sites under room-temperature tensile deformation.
generation.intervention: Incorporation of a minor microalloying element (Nb) into the alloy composition combined with a thermal treatment designed to drive Nb segregation to the internal boundaries.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature tensile deformation after thermal processing optimized for promoting Nb segregation; the Nb addition is maintained at a low concentration (below 1 wt%) to avoid excessive precipitation.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of Nb-enriched boundary regions and nanoscale precipitates at internal colony boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Nb atoms preferentially segregate to the internal boundaries during the tailored thermal treatment, enhancing interfacial cohesion which delays microcrack initiation. Simultaneously, the nanoscale Nb-rich precipitates contribute to precipitation strengthening within the lamellar structure.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the conventional eutectic high-entropy alloy, the Nb-modified alloy is expected to show increased tensile strength and enhanced ductility at room temperature, evidenced by a lower microcrack density along the lamellar boundaries.
generation.baseline: Conventional eutectic high-entropy alloys processed without Nb addition, which exhibit brittleness mainly due to the early initiation of microcracks at internal boundaries.
generation.boundary: The improvement is anticipated to be effective only within a narrow Nb concentration range (below 1 wt%) and under specific thermal processing conditions. The mechanism is assumed to be applicable primarily to eutectic alloys with dual-phase lamellar morphologies and may not extend to non-eutectic or single-phase alloys.
generation.uncertainty: There remains uncertainty regarding the optimal Nb concentration and detailed thermal processing parameters required to achieve effective boundary segregation and the precise balance between precipitation strengthening and ductility enhancement.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of eutectic high-entropy alloy samples: one set processed conventionally without Nb and a second set with a controlled addition of Nb (below 1 wt%) followed by thermal processing aimed at promoting Nb segregation. Conduct room-temperature tensile tests and perform microstructural characterization (using SEM, TEM, and elemental mapping) on both sets.
measurements: Density and spatial distribution of microcracks at lamellar boundaries
Verification of Nb segregation at the internal boundaries through elemental mapping
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Nb-modified samples do not show statistically significant improvements in both tensile strength and ductility compared to the conventional alloy, or if microstructural analysis does not confirm notable Nb segregation with a concomitant reduction in microcrack density, then the hypothesis is falsified.
